subject: Mathematics
source: Original supplementary learning draft aligned to Class 6 Ganita Prakash Chapter 7 (fegp107.pdf), Reprint 2026–27. Verify any school-specific edition before publication.
goals: Recognise equivalent fractions and simplify them.
Compare fractions using equal denominators or a common denominator.
Add and subtract fractions with compatible denominators.
summary: A fraction represents equal parts of a whole or a quantity. The denominator tells how many equal parts make one whole; the numerator tells how many of those parts are being considered. Equivalent fractions name the same value in different forms.

concepts.title: Meaning of a fraction
concepts.explanation: A fraction a/b describes a parts when a whole is divided into b equal parts, with b not zero. The parts must be equal for the fraction model to be valid.
concepts.example: 3/4 means three of four equal parts.

concepts.title: Equivalent fractions
concepts.explanation: Multiplying or dividing numerator and denominator by the same non-zero number gives an equivalent fraction. The value remains unchanged because the ratio is unchanged.

concepts.title: Comparing fractions
concepts.explanation: With the same denominator, the fraction with the larger numerator is larger. With different denominators, express fractions using a common denominator or compare them using a clear model.
concepts.example: 3/8 < 5/8 because both fractions describe eighths and 3 parts are fewer than 5 parts.

concepts.title: Adding and subtracting
concepts.explanation: When denominators are the same, add or subtract numerators and keep the denominator. With different denominators, first rewrite the fractions with a common denominator.

workedExamples.question: Simplify 12/18.
steps: Find a common factor of 12 and 18; 6 divides both.

workedExamples.question: Calculate 1/4 + 1/6.
steps: A common denominator for 4 and 6 is 12.

practice.question: Write an equivalent fraction for 2/3 with denominator 12.
Why can’t you simply add the denominators when adding fractions?
practice.answer: The denominator names the size of the equal parts; adding denominators would change the unit of the parts rather than count how many parts are combined.
practice.why: Use equal-sized parts before adding numerators.

mcqs.why: The denominator is the bottom number, 8.
All denominators are 9; 5 is the largest numerator.

mcqs.q: A common denominator for 1/2 and 1/5 is…

revision: Numerator counts parts; denominator tells the number of equal parts in one whole.
Equivalent fractions have the same value.
For the same denominator, compare numerators.
Use a common denominator before adding or subtracting unlike fractions.
Simplify a fraction by dividing numerator and denominator by a common factor.

chapterTest.instructions: Answer independently before opening the answer guide. Show steps for calculations.

questions.q: Compare 2/3 and 3/5 using a common denominator.
questions.answer: Common denominator 15: 2/3=10/15 and 3/5=9/15, so 2/3 is greater.
